title: 2025 HMMT February Guts Problem 1
statement: Call a 9-digit number a _cassowary_ if it uses each of the digits 1 through 9 exactly once. Compute the number of cassowaries that are prime.

solutions.text: Every cassowary is divisible by 3, as the sum of its digits is \(1 + 2 + \dots + 9 = 45\) . Since all such numbers are divisible by 3 and and greater than 3, none of them are prime. So, there are 0 prime cassowaries.
